Practical tools: audit giving vs taking; distinguish jealousy (fear of loss) from envy (desire to take/destroy); set healthy-boundaries-relationships via self-inquiry (friend walking in unannounced example); use mentalization before conflict resolution; recognize when there is no us and exit exploitative bonds; repair the broken-compass-self-map before latching onto another person's unhealthy map. Power dynamics, anxiety, and communication protocols framed through conscious/unconscious mind interaction between two people.
key_insights: Healthiest self in relationships — Show up with maximum agency-and-gratitude; relationships amplify structure/function of self, not replace inner work.
Generative drive matching — Romantic success correlates with partners whose generative drives are strong and compatible; aggressive/pleasure drives should subserve generative drive, not dominate.
Trauma bonds reframed — Not inherently bad; two people bonded through shared trauma can heal together if both work toward generative living; pathology when trauma keeps bond exploitative.
Libido as generative expression — Sexual energy in healthy partnerships reflects generative giving/receiving; avoidance often signals unprocessed barriers, not mere preference.
Repetition compulsion — Fourth abusive relationship in a row = unconscious pattern, not bad luck; requires ten-cupboards-exercise before choosing again.
Narcissism + dependence — Exploitative character structure draws pathological dependence; demoralization on one side, bottomless need on other; not a fixable "us" without individual work.
Jealousy ≠ envy — Jealousy = fear of losing something valued; envy = entitled taking/destruction (walking into friend's house to ruin privacy); envy lens predicts exploitation.
Giving vs taking audit — Healthy relationships trend generative-giving; chronic taking without reciprocity signals no real "us."
Transactions vs relationships — Kindergarten-level tit-for-tat ("you didn't share your snack") is not adult relating; flexibility and generative intent matter.
Anxiety in relationships — Communicate from self-awareness; if activated/triggered, defer conflict ("can we talk later?") — last time to make conclusions when you can't mentalize.
Magic bridge of the us — Me + you + shared generative space; when you feel "us" but they don't, immense power in recognizing mismatch and self-protecting.
Mentalization order — Start with me (map/cupboards), then you, then us; thinking about other before self = fool's errand; mentalization greases all progress.
Broken compass — Unexplored self-map drifts; latching onto another's unhealthy map when yours is blurry; fix your map to find others who've done the work.
Work relationships — Oppression, accountability, envy in colleagues; same framework applies beyond romance.

videos.title: Build Muscle Size, Increase Strength & Improve Recovery | Huberman Lab Essentials
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman Huberman Lab Essentials recap (~28 min, 1.1M views) distilling the full build-strength-muscle-endurance-andy-galpin episode (and prior muscle-science content) into actionable resistance-training, recovery, and nutrition tools. Thesis: muscle is longevity infrastructure — governed by upper/lower motor neurons and central pattern generators — and adaptation happens after training, not during it.

Covers: henneman-size-principle (motor-unit recruitment staircases from low to high threshold; heavy weights are *not* required for hypertrophy); three muscle stimuli (stress, tension, damage); mind-muscle-intentionality — strength = move load as a system, hypertrophy = isolate hard local contractions; 30–80% 1RM as the evidence-backed load band; 5 sets/week minimum to maintain, 5–15 sets/week to improve (advanced up to ~25–30); ~10% of sets to failure so most volume stays sub-max (eighty-twenty-exercise-rule); 2-min rest for testosterone protocol work, 2–6 min for hypertrophy/strength; explosiveness at 60–75% 1RM with fast concentric; recovery gauges — morning grip strength and carbon-dioxide-discard-rate; cold-heat-exercise-timing / nsaid-exercise-interference — post-lift ice and NSAIDs within ±4 h blunt mTOR-driven gains; salt/electrolytes for nerve firing; creatine-monohydrate (~5 g/day; 12–20% power output in studies); leucine-protein-density (700–3,000 mg leucine per meal from whole foods).

Best use: quick protocol reference before committing to the 211-min Galpin masterclass; pairs creatine-fat-loss-secret-darren-candow for supplement depth.
key_insights: Nervous system controls muscle — Upper motor neurons (deliberate), lower motor neurons (acetylcholine → contraction), central pattern generators (rhythmic/reflexive walking).
Heavy weights optional for most people — 30–80% 1RM builds strength and size; extreme strength may still need heavy loads.
Hypertrophy vs strength focus — Can you independently contract each muscle? Better isolation → fewer sets needed; strength = progressive load, hypertrophy = painful localized contraction.
Volume prescription — ≥5 sets/muscle/week at 30–80% 1RM just to maintain; 5–15 to improve (2–20 range in literature); advanced trainers up to 25–30 if recoverable.
Failure sparingly — ~10% of sets/workouts to failure preserves volume capacity; most sets sub-max.
Rest intervals — ~2 min (Duncan French testosterone protocol); 2–6 min for hypertrophy/strength sets.
Recovery tests (morning, zero cost) — Grip force drop ≥10–20% = systemic nerve-to-muscle fatigue; CO2 discard <25–30 s = not recovered, 30–60 s = green zone, 65–120 s = nervous system ready.
Don't short-circuit adaptation — Post-resistance ice baths and NSAIDs ±4 h around training interfere with inflammation-driven repair (mTOR pathway).
Salt + creatine + leucine — Sodium enables neuronal firing; creatine hydrates cells and boosts power; leucine from protein-dense meals (2–4 meals/day).

videos.title: Build & Sell with Claude Code (10+ Hour Course)
videos.creator: nate-herk
videos.summary:
Nate Herk's flagship 10-hour beginner-to-pro Claude Code course (774K+ views). Unlike the shorter AIOS course, this video starts from absolute zero — terminal setup, tokens, CLAUDE.md, and the WAT framework (Workflows, Agent, Tools) — then walks through building real automations, deploying them, and monetizing the skills.

The first half is hands-on building: newsletter automation (Perplexity research → HTML → infographics → Gmail), a second workflow, deployment to run 24/7, project architecture, RAG, turning n8n flows into apps, website hacks, APIs/MCPs, Google Workspace CLI, and a personal executive assistant. The second half goes deeper on skills, sub-agents, agent teams, browser automation, permissions, GitHub worktrees, and "fun hacks." The final ~90 minutes cover the business side: selling mindset, finding clients, first client in 7 days, value-based pricing, and project delivery.

Core thesis: agentic workflows are the future ($7B → ~$93B market), but n8n/Zapier fundamentals still matter — you need to understand plumbing to spot bad agent decisions. During interactive builds, agents self-heal; once deployed (workflows + tools only, not the live agent), behavior becomes more deterministic — battle-test before shipping.
key_insights: WAT framework — Workflows are natural-language markdown recipes; Tools are Python scripts (ingredients); the Agent (Claude Code) reads workflows and invokes tools in order. Both improve over time as the agent learns from mistakes.
Plan mode first — Switch to plan mode for ambiguous requests; Claude asks clarifying questions before building. Read and edit the plan before auto-accepting.
`.env` for secrets — Never paste API keys into chat; store Perplexity, Gmail, etc. in `.env` placeholders the agent creates.
Self-healing vs deployment — Live agent sessions can debug mid-run; deployed automations (GitHub → trigger.dev/modal/Vercel) run workflows + tools without the agent — test heavily before deploy.

Five Claude Code surfaces — Terminal (most power), desktop app (GUI + scheduled tasks), web at claude.ai/code (persists when laptop off), IDE extensions (VS Code/Cursor/Antigravity), each wrapping the same engine.
Skills = loadable SOPs — Front-end design skill, custom infographic skill, etc.; agent decides when to invoke based on description matching the task.
Sub-agents & agent teams — Delegate subtasks to specialized agents; teams coordinate parallel work (CLI-only features like `/agents`).
Doctor, not pharmacist — Sell diagnosis and ROI ("save 20 hrs/week"), not "I build Claude Code workflows." Avoid hourly pricing once value is proven.
Value-based pricing example — System saves client $10K/month → charge $5K for build; payback in two weeks for them, strong margin for you.
API reference docs often beat MCP — Research once, save endpoints locally; lower token burn than loading full MCP tool schemas every session.

videos.title: Build & Sell Claude Code Operating Systems (2+ Hour Course)
videos.creator: nate-herk
videos.summary:
Nate Herk delivers a comprehensive 2.5-hour course on building a personal AI Operating System (AIOS) inside Claude Code. The core thesis: treat Claude Code as your primary workspace layer — with agents, skills, and connections on top — so you can stay in one interface instead of context-switching across dozens of apps.

The course walks through two foundational frameworks. The Three Ms (Mindset, Method, Machine) shape how you think about AI leverage: default to asking "how could AI do 30% of this?", break jobs into automatable chunks, and treat AI as a mentor rather than a vending machine. The Four Cs (Context, Connections, Capabilities, Cadence) define the durable setup order for an AIOS — you cannot skip steps; cadence requires connections, capabilities require context.

Practically, Nate clones a free GitHub template repo into VS Code, runs an onboarding skill (7-question interview), wires ClickUp via API reference docs (preferring API over MCP for token efficiency), sets up Google Workspace CLI, builds custom skills from SOPs, and layers on scheduled automation via cloud routines, local scheduled tasks, and the /loop skill. He also covers Karpathy's LLM wiki pattern for compounding knowledge (Obsidian visualization) and Claude Co-work live artifacts for lightweight dashboards.
key_insights: Productivity dips before it climbs — expect ~20% short-term loss when adopting an AIOS; exponential learning curve pays off by week two.
Tool-agnostic durable layer — build context files, API reference markdown, and skills that survive model/tool churn; Nate migrated his AIOS to Codex in ~2 minutes.
API reference docs beat MCP for token efficiency — research an integration once, save endpoints as local markdown; hardcode frequently used IDs in skills after watching agent behavior.
Dedicated AI service accounts — create separate API keys/accounts (e.g., "Up AI" in ClickUp) with scoped permissions instead of using your full-access personal credentials.

Skills are SOPs for agents — `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML front matter; progressive disclosure loads name/description first (~100 tokens), full skill on invoke, references/scripts only when needed.
Cadence has three tiers — cloud routines (GitHub repo + env vars, runs with laptop off), desktop scheduled tasks (local/remote), and `/loop` (same-session cron, 3-day expiry, minutely intervals).
Proof of concept before custom dashboards — start with Claude artifacts; only build custom refresh pipelines if you actually use the visualization daily.
Deterministic workflows often beat agents — break processes into chunks; many chunks need boring automation, not autonomous AI.
Success criteria (subjective KPIs) — team could ask your AIOS instead of you; you stop opening new tabs; knowledge leaves your head.

videos.title: Dr. Andy Galpin: How to Build Strength, Muscle Size & Endurance
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman hosts andy-galpin (~211 min, 10.4M views) for a masterclass in exercise science spanning nine trainable adaptations — skill, speed, power, strength, hypertrophy, muscular endurance, anaerobic power, VO2 max, and long-duration endurance. Galpin's core thesis: concepts are few, methods are many. Exercise choice does not determine adaptation; modifiable-variables-strength-conditioning (sets, reps, intensity, rest, frequency) does. For strength, the three-by-five-strength-protocol (3–5 exercises × 3–5 reps × 3–5 sets × 3–5 min rest × 3–5 days/week at 85%+ 1RM) is a flexible template; power uses the same structure at 40–70% with velocity emphasis. Hypertrophy is "idiot-proof" on programming but hard on execution: 5–30 reps per set to near failure, volume drives growth, vary rep schemes for engagement. mind-muscle-intentionality — move weight for strength, challenge the target muscle for hypertrophy.

Endurance gets a weekly kit: 150–180 min zone 2 (conversational pace; does not block hypertrophy), once/week VO2-max touch (4–8 bouts of ~90 sec near max HR; every other week minimum), and 2–6 min hard repeats at ~80% HR (mile-repeat logic). Start concentric-dominant modalities (bike, row, sled) to avoid eccentric soreness from jumping into running. Hydration via the galpin-equation-hydration; cold-heat-exercise-timing — cold blunts adaptation if overused during hypertrophy blocks (use pre-training or 4+ hr away; morning cold can improve HRV); post-lift sauna may plausibly aid hypertrophy. Recovery = visible stressors + hidden stressors vs stress-recovery-capacity-balance; grip strength and CO2 tolerance as practical gauges. Supplements: creatine-monohydrate ("Michael Jordan" of supplements), sodium bicarbonate, beta-alanine.
key_insights: Nine adaptations, fat loss is a byproduct — Train the outcome you want; pushing one adaptation can sacrifice another.
Exercise ≠ adaptation — Bench press can build endurance or strength depending on rep range, speed, and rest; beginners should pick simpler movements.
Strength: intensity drives; hypertrophy: volume drives — Min ~2×/week per muscle for strength; hypertrophy needs enough sets taken close to failure.
Hypertrophy rep range 5–30 — All equally effective if near failure; drivers are mechanical tension, metabolic stress, and some muscle damage (more soreness ≠ more growth).
3×5 concept for strength/power — Scales from 20-min/week minimal to full five-day programs; change load % for power vs strength.
Zone 2 + intervals don't kill gains — Conversational cardio may help hypertrophy via blood flow; HIIT near max HR is complementary, not substitutive.
Point of physiological failure — Where you quit (legs vs lungs) tells you what to train; same VO2 max can mask different limiters.
Breathing down-regulation post-hard work — 3+ min exhale-emphasis breathing after intervals; saves neural energy for life outside training.
Galpin equation — Body weight (lb) ÷ 30 = oz fluid per 15 min exercise/cognition baseline; add ~1 g sodium per liter sweat in heat/long sessions.
Creatine monohydrate — Strong safety profile; benefits beyond muscle (clinical/neurological research); 5 g/day standard for most.

videos.title: Cancer Scientist: This Common Daily Diet May Be Feeding Cancer!
videos.creator: steven-bartlett
videos.summary:
the-diary-of-a-ceo return interview (~106 min) with Boston College professor thomas-seyfried — metabolic oncology researcher arguing that cancer is primarily a cancer-mitochondrial-metabolic-disease, not a genetic disease of the nucleus. Host steven-bartlett opens with an embargoed *Frontiers in Science* paper Seyfried frames as a lead strategy to manage cancer with less toxicity, then pivots to prevention and actionable lifestyle.

Core lineage: otto-warburg (1920s–40s) showed cancer cells ferment glucose even in oxygen (Warburg effect); Seyfried extends this — damaged mitochondria force compensatory fermentation on glucose + glutamine; DNA mutations and ROS are largely *downstream* of organelle damage. nuclear-cytoplasm-cancer-transfer experiments: cancer nucleus in healthy cytoplasm → no cancer; healthy nucleus in cancer cytoplasm → cancer — cytoplasm/mitochondria decide fate, not the mutational load alone. Critique of somatic mutation theory: driver mutations appear in normal non-cancer cells; many tumors lack clear driver mutations ("wild-type cancers").

Actionable stack: glucose-ketone-index-gki as mitochondrial-health biomarker (low glucose + elevated ketones); bioenergetic-prevention-zones (yellow/green = Paleolithic-like prevention; red = high sugar/low ketones = disease risk); therapeutic ketosis + fasting to "sanitize" tumors before lower-dose chemo; press-pulse-cancer-therapy (press glucose down, pulse glutamine with agents like mebendazole). Diet is bioenergetic, not tribal — calorie-restricted Mediterranean (fish, olive oil, avocado + exercise) or carefully disciplined carnivore can both lower GKI; refined carbs/HFCS worst. Case vignette: Pablo Kelly (Devon) lived ~10 years with glioblastoma on metabolic therapy alone; died of surgical hemorrhage, not tumor. Environment: PFAS/microplastics/glyphosate/heavy metals damage oxidative phosphorylation → compensatory glucose/glutamine use. Founding more-alliance (Metabolic Oncology Research and Education) at boston-college to organize metabolic + conventional care.

Strong complement to anti-aging-gray-hair-youth-energy-martin-picard-doac / martin-picard energy-first disease frame — Seyfried is the clinical oncology / Warburg-continuation lane; Picard is the psychobiology / energy-resistance lane. Also pairs david-unwin-fatty-liver-metabolic-health-doac (glucose load / metabolic disease) and ketogenic-diet-mental-health (ketones as alternative fuel).
key_insights: Cancer origin = mitochondrial damage — structure determines function; "ghost mitochondria" under EM; field still treats mutations as primary
~1,700 US cancer deaths/day — Seyfried's urgency framing; incidence still rising (breast, prostate, pancreatic, melanoma, HPV oral)
Dog vs wolf — domestic dogs #1 killer cancer; wild wolves rare — lifestyle/food/inactivity as mitochondrial insult analogy
Dual fuel — glucose (glycolysis) + glutamine (glutaminolysis); must restrict both; ketones feed healthy cells, not corrupted tumor mitochondria
GKI — built after Trudy Dupont brainstem-tumor case (~10+ years); ratio tool for prevention and management
Zones — yellow/green hard to get cancer; red zone → must drop to green for management, then drug-target glutamine
Press-pulse (with Dominic D'Agostino, Joe Maroon) — press glucose (diet/fasting), pulse glutamine (repurposed drugs)
Chemo/radiation as pulse, not first hammer — ketosis + fasting protect healthy cells; lower targeted doses after metabolic prep
Not "cure" language — manage, extend life, make tumors indolent; glioblastoma still deadly but metabolic results claimed vs 100-year stagnation
Lifestyle prescription — cut ultraprocessed carbs, move, sleep, lower emotional stress; individualize macros for GKI; avoid HFCS; seed oils secondary/uncertain
Carcinogens converge — forever chemicals, microplastics, arsenic/cadmium in water → OXPHOS damage → fermentation shift
Scientific literacy — population demand + published case reports will shift oncology; foundation support asked for metabolic research

videos.title: \"ChatGPT Moment\" for Robotics Is Coming. The Real Problem Isn't Intelligence | Stanford, Catie Cuan
videos.creator: catie-cuan
videos.summary:
catie-cuan (~19 min, Stanford Robotics Center) argues the robotics field is entering a "ChatGPT moment" — weekly breakthrough announcements and a path to billions of robots in everyday spaces (offices, hospitals, hotels, homes) on an iPhone-like adoption curve (~13 years to 1B devices). But the missing layer is not raw intelligence; it is human-interaction-robotics-grand-challenge — how humans and robots become human-robot-legibility to one another when unpredictable people share space with increasingly capable machines.

Cuan's background bridges dance, art, and engineering: professional dancer → Google artist-in-residence → founder of art-lab (AI Robot Technology) and researcher at stanford-robotics-center. Her father's hospital experience — surrounded by life-saving but opaque, oppressive beeping machines — crystallized a humanistic robotics mission: machines that empower, delight, and feel legible, not merely utilitarian.

Technical contribution: vision-language-interaction-model-vli — a model class that takes behavioral impetus from humans in the environment (like LLMs on human text), maps to robot actions, and judges success by human response (positive/negative affect). This closes the loop on social robotics beyond task completion.

Cultural critique: the field is humanoid-uncanny-expectations-locked — human-shaped robots in human spaces raise mirror-neuron expectations they cannot meet (rodney-brooks). Cuan advocates robots-beyond-utility-paradigm — companionship (Paro seal), autism social-skills aids, art/dance — not only humanoids doing dishes. Her Google robot-music-mode-google project (200 robots' motion data → symphony) proved engineers wanted robot-delight-experiences, not ambivalence toward "fine" utility bots.

Pedagogy: Stanford CS 334 Robots and Arts teaches why-before-what-building in an era of infinite build opportunity — finite-time-resource-allocation demands knowing values before spending irreplaceable time. Aristotle's homo-technae-tool-relationship frames robots as the latest link in humanity's tool continuum, while years of debugging left Cuan more awed by human dexterity and expressiveness than any machine.
key_insights: Intelligence ≠ interaction — robotics hype centers capability; the hard problem is unpredictable humans in shared spaces
Billions-of-robots timeline — iPhone hit 1B in ~13 years; robotics workforce + capital suggests similar density in lifetimes
VLI model — first model class measuring robot action success via human affect response, not just task metrics
Hospital opacity lesson — life-support machines that beep without explanation traumatize vulnerable patients; legibility is safety + dignity
Google music mode — mapping joint motion → musical samples turned "fine" office robots into crying-at-desk awe experiences; shipped fleet-wide
Rodney Brooks humanoid trap — human-likeness raises expectations via mirror neurons; 77-year-old ESL dad may not want a humanoid even if it works
Beyond dirty/dull/dangerous — Paro seal companions, autism social robots show non-humanoid beneficial roles already exist
2017 transcendent dance — first choreography with a robot felt like Homo technae continuum from stone tools to modern machines
Humans > robots expressively — years of robotics work increased respect for human diversity of motion, timing, social acuity
Mark Skylar Scott 25-year heart — worthy crafts take a lifetime; robotics needs problems worth that dedication
CS 334 why-question — when building is easy/infinite, the scarce resource is *why* you build — values + time allocation
Time unscalable — only resource equal for everyone; cannot buy back; building choices = spending precious time

videos.title: China Doesn't Need Better AI to Beat America | Stanford China Researcher, Dan Wang
videos.creator: dan-wang
videos.summary:
dan-wang (~17 min) — author of *Breakneck: China's Quest to Engineer the Future*, research fellow at hoover-institution, former technology analyst at gavekal-dragonomics — argues that ai-magical-thinking-geopolitics in Silicon Valley and Washington overweights AI model sophistication as a decisive US-China strategic advantage. The US has at best a ai-moderate-lead-not-decisive over China on AI; Chinese firms have produced excellent models despite ~decade of export controls, often open-source and cheaply run, with some video-generation models arguably ahead.

The deeper competition axis is physical dynamism, not labs: China china-infrastructure-outbuilding-us — ~300 GW solar vs ~30 GW US last year, 40 nuclear plants under construction vs zero in the US, ~1,500 ships vs ~5, auto model iteration ~18 months vs 5–6 years American. china-manufacturing-ecosystem-advantage — dark factories, dense supplier networks, ~70M manufacturing workers across skill tiers — may matter more than marginal model quality gains.

China's engineering-state-vs-social-engineering built subways, high-speed rail (2× rest of world combined), bridges, and power — but engineers also social-engineered the one-child policy (~300M abortions, ~100M sterilizations over 35 years) when leadership treated population as building material. anaconda-censorship-metaphor (Perry Link) — self-censorship without visible enforcement — corrodes creative thinking; Wang's own site was blocked in 2022.

us-china-self-sabotage-dynamic: whichever country leads makes hubris mistakes; the trailing country feels the whip. Xi Jinping's 2021 property-sector demolition and tech crackdown (Jack Ma) caused today's economic drag; Trump's tariffs, alliance erosion, and deporting ~300 South Korean engineers from a Georgia Hyundai EV plant hurt US manufacturing credibility. Wang's message to both: do less. In 10 years, made-in-china-quality-premium — "Made in China" may rival Germany/Japan quality labels as manufacturing concentrates in China.
key_insights: US AI lead is moderate not decisive — China catching up quickly; export controls haven't prevented competitive models
Deployment infrastructure > model sophistication — electrical power, factories, iteration speed determine who benefits from AI rollout
China built 1,500 ships last year; US built ~5 — industrial capacity gap dwarfs AI benchmark gaps
Dark factories — lights off, minimal human workers — plus dense ecosystem of battery/sensor/EV suppliers next door
Engineer-led state excels at physical infrastructure; fails when it social-engineers people (one-child policy)
Anaconda in chandelier — censorship works through ambient fear, not constant visible punishment
Both countries self-sabotage — leader overconfidence (Xi property smash, Trump tariffs/deportations) vs trailing-country urgency
Don't trade vibrant manufacturing ecosystem for marginally better AI models
Silicon Valley founders inspirational but don't deliver orderly streets, affordable housing, clean cities to ordinary Americans
Young workers in AI-exposed jobs seeing 16% slower employment growth — opportunity if augmented not automated
Made in China brand trajectory → premium quality parity with Germany/Japan within a decade

videos.title: I Turned Claude Into a 24/7 Trader
videos.creator: nate-herk
videos.summary:
Nate Herk migrates his Bull trading agent from OpenClaw to Claude Code remote routines powered by Opus 4.7. The bot researches markets, places trades via Alpaca, journals into markdown memory files, and sends daily recaps to ClickUp — with no always-on Python process. Claude *is* the bot.

The build follows six steps: (1) define strategy (beat the S&P, fundamentals over day trading), (2) scaffold a GitHub-backed project, (3) guardrails, (4) skills, (5) five weekday routines, (6) deploy to cloud with env vars. Prior OpenClaw run: $10K live Alpaca, ~8% ahead of S&P in 30 days. Migration exports strategy, trade log, research log, and learnings into the new repo via plan mode + brainstorming.

The mental model: each routine wakes stateless (~200K token budget per run). Discipline and learning live in files — read memory first, execute, write back, commit to main so the next run inherits state. Remote routines clone the repo, work, destroy the cloud instance; persistence requires explicit git push with allow unrestricted branch pushes enabled.
key_insights: Opus 4.7 + routines = 24/7 agent — full agentic loop on a schedule; cheaper than equivalent API-only cron orchestration at Nate's usage level.
Genetic financial analysis ≠ day trading — benchmark rewards fundamentals/thesis writing; maps to long-term or swing strategies, not candlestick timing.
Five weekday crons — pre-market (research, draft ideas), market open (execute + 10% trailing stops), midday (cut −7% losers, tighten winners), close (EOD summary), Friday weekly review.
Start paper, phase up — like teaching a kid to ride a bike; guardrails before autonomy (max % per position, daily loss cap, no options, position limits).
Env var names must match exactly — cloud environment keys (e.g. `ALPACA_API_SECRET`) must appear letter-for-letter in prompts; agent defaulted to `.env` and failed until fixed.
Never commit secrets — rotate keys found in migrated OpenClaw templates; store Alpaca, Perplexity, ClickUp keys in Claude Desktop cloud environment settings only.
Files = personality + discipline — not just memory; orchestrate which files each routine reads (strategy, trade log, `CLAUDE.md` ~156 lines for Bull).
Watch every run early — read conversation history, tweak prompts and context files; agent suggests skill updates in daily insights.
Context reset before routine design — `/clear` with pasted session summary after migration to avoid rot before planning crons.
Perplexity over native web search — preferred research API; keys from env vars at runtime.

videos.title: I asked Claude Code to make me as much money as possible
videos.creator: nate-herk
videos.summary:
Nate Herk claims four Claude Code upgrades 3×'d his income in 30 days by fixing design flaws that make Claude feel productive but not profitable. Income is capped by output quality and production speed — not raw intelligence. The video walks through all four upgrades live on a demo business: a $9/mo tool that turns YouTube transcripts into a week of LinkedIn posts (rebranded "Cadence" after validation).

Upgrade 1 — Stop sycophancy: Claude defaults to agreement mode ("yes man"). The /roast skill spins up a council of sub-agents (contrarian, expansionist, first-principles thinker, deep researcher, buyer, judge) that stress-test ideas before building. Verdict: green light, reshape, or kill — plus the cheapest 48-hour validation test. On the demo idea, the council scored it 2–8/10 and recommended reshape: kill the commodity $9 wrapper, keep the engine, target a narrow niche with voice matching + scheduled posting.

Upgrade 2 — Verification loop: "Finished" ≠ working. ~40% of Copilot-generated code had vulnerabilities (NYU study). Nate's outreach agent claimed 100% email delivery but only sent 25%. Fix: make Claude verify before handing off, then stress-test after. Live demo: landing page built with Playwright CLI screenshots at desktop + mobile viewports, iterated until zero visible errors, then 22 form-submission stress tests (valid + malformed inputs) in a headed browser.

Upgrade 3 — Context management: "Context rot" degrades all 18 tested models as conversations lengthen — well before the window fills. Nate prefers /session-handoff over /compact, then /clear + paste. Handoff captures decisions locked, shipped files, running state, open questions, and "pick up here." Uses status line to stay under ~250K tokens; /context to audit what's eating tokens.

Upgrade 4 — Sub-agents + /goal: Anthropic's parallel sub-agent team beat a single agent by >90% on internal evals. /goal sets an objective completion condition; a separate evaluator model grades each turn so the worker can't declare itself done. Final demo: 6 parallel sub-agents built a full go-to-market kit in ~8 minutes (positioning, market research, launch plan, outreach templates, drafts, content calendar) — stacking all four upgrades.
key_insights: Productive ≠ profitable — Claude is tuned for agreement and completion feelings, not business outcomes.
AI sycophancy is measured — "Elephant" study: models fail to push back on framing ~88% of the time (humans ~60%); personalization/memory makes it worse.
Council beats single-perspective advice — side-by-side demo: plain Claude gave generic "rework it" feedback; roast council gave scored personas, CAC/LTV analysis, and a concrete 48-hour test.
Verification is a habit, not one button — define "done" per domain; build loop (create → verify → fix → repeat); then adversarial stress testing.
First shot ~65%, verification gets ~90% — same benchmark Cole Medin cites; less human rework on review.
Context rot starts early — longer conversations make Claude dumber even on simple tasks; more context is not better.
Session handoff > compact — Nate finds `/compact` slow; custom handoff skill preserves state across `/clear` and enables cross-tool transfer (e.g. to Codex).
Parallel sub-agents for independent work — each gets a clean context window; synthesize after.
`/goal` separates worker from judge — addresses the same sycophancy problem at completion time; objective done-criteria work best.
Role shift: builder → reviewer — with all four upgrades, human becomes problem-solver, decision-maker, and judge.
Skills available free in ai-automation-society Skool community (roast, session handoff).

videos.title: I Spent 2 Billion Tokens Vibe Coding With Claude Opus 4.8
videos.creator: bridgemind
videos.summary:
bridgemind (~17 min, 21.4K views, May 2026) stress-tests claude-opus-4-8 after spending 2B+ tokens in two days — 480M fast mode, 973M + 655M in Claude Code, plus a third Claude Max subscription for ultra-code. Context: Opus 4.8 shipped six weeks after 4.7 (fastest Opus cadence ever) amid Anthropic losing search-volume share to OpenAI Codex post-GPT 5.5.

key_insights: Opus 4.8 released 6 weeks after 4.7 — fastest Opus turnaround; vidIQ shows Claude Code search volume falling (~8.8M → under 6M) while Codex rising (~1.8M → 3M).
Creator frames release as Anthropic rushing to win back share after 4.7 miss; users still preferred 4.6.
Same knowledge cutoff (Jan 2026), same hallucination rate, same output-token profile as 4.7 — suggests incremental tuning not new frontier.
SWE-Bench Pro gains dismissed as contaminated/open-source benchmark.
Intelligence index #1 but CursorBench regression on ambiguous multi-file agent tasks.
BridgeBench: lava lamp worse than 4.7; security, refactoring, debugging regressions.
Single-shot HTML FPS game (map, kill feed, RPG effects) better than prior Opus — but "not real software."
ultra-code runs phased workflows (classify → verify → …) with many parallel sub-agents; extremely token-hungry (1.6B tokens in Claude Code in one day).
Demo: 105 agents optimizing BridgeSpace cross-OS performance → shipped to production → introduced terminal text-rendering bug.
8 automated fix attempts failed across Opus 4.8 variants; manual revert required.
Parallel UltraCode during video: 15 agents classify phase; 9% of one $200 Max plan used by two agents over ~14 min.
Promotion videos (BridgeSpace, Bridge Swarm pages), Bridge Voice page redesign — marketing/content generation solid since ~4.6.
Incremental UI polish (terminal header hover/responsiveness) — "normal" capability for ~6 months, not a leap.
Anthropic announced Mythos-class models for all customers "in coming weeks."
Polymarket Claude Mythos by end of June jumped ~10% → ~40%.
Creator waiting for model that fixes hard production bugs, not just ships pretty demos.

videos.title: I Turned Claude Into the Ultimate Second Brain
videos.creator: nate-herk
videos.summary:
Nate Herk walks through his live Herk 2 AIOS — months in the making — stress-tested with Claude Fable (Anthropic's limited-release Mythos-class model). The video is less a build tutorial than a day-in-the-life tour: mindset, folder architecture, how the Four Cs map onto his actual files, and usage habits that make the system compound.

Core distinction: second brain = knowledge (Context + Connections in the Four Cs); AIOS = infrastructure on top (Capabilities + Cadence). An OS starts with a default harness (Claude Code), not architecture. CLAUDE.md is the routing tree — wiki paths, hot cache, master index, skills, sub-agents, API key locations. An other worlds folder nests frequently used repos (YouTube OS, book, website) inside Herk 2 for GitHub sync and cross-project context. At ~40k tokens on /context, scale has not been a problem yet; pulse check is whether *you* and the agent can find files intuitively without long searches.

Fable demos include a one-prompt /goal journey video and a 21-minute one-shot interactive concept map from YouTube transcripts. Usage tips: thought partner (devil's advocate, sub-agent debates), grill me skill for knowledge extraction, and verify own work (Playwright, persona testing). Cadence requires earned trust via keys, not prompts — illustrated by a mistaken bulk email to 150–200k subscribers.
key_insights: Close the tabs, default to one harness — repeating yourself across ChatGPT projects/custom GPTs ≠ having a co-founder who knows your business.
Second brain before AIOS — knowledge layer first; skills/automation/cadence build on top.
Four Cs split — Context + Connections = second brain; Capabilities + Cadence = AIOS infrastructure.
CLAUDE.md as router — points to rules, references, skills, wikis, other projects; architecture engineering is its own craft.
Other worlds folder — nest active repos inside main AIOS for single-repo sync and unified agent reach.
Static vs live data — markdown/wiki for background; APIs/CLIs for changing data (subscriber count example: stale 620k vs live 800k).
Tier-one connection heuristic — weekly apps/bookmarks/comms → revenue, customers, calendar, tasks, meetings, knowledge.
Skills iterate forever — turn repeated prompts into skills; every run is feedback data; no finished product.
Assembly-line sessions — research → `/clear` → draft → `/clear` → polish; one AI, one job per phase.
Delegate on Fable — expensive model for orchestration; Sonnet/Haiku for parallel sub-tasks.
Earn cadence — battle-test skills first; automation raises cost, risk, and maintenance; triggers = manual, event, or schedule.
Keys not prompts — scoped API keys are the real permission layer; "if it can, it will."
Tool-agnostic IP — folders, markdown, skills, routing logic survive model/harness churn (Codex, Sonnet, future open models).
Fable economics — ~2× Opus pricing ($10/M in, $50/M out); can burn $200/mo Max 5-hour window in ~1 hour under stress test; cyber guardrails sometimes over-trigger at launch.

videos.title: How to Control Your Cortisol & Overcome Burnout | Huberman Lab
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman full episode (~136 min, 653K views) on cortisol-rhythm-24hr — reframing cortisol not as a "stress hormone" but as an energy-deployment hormone (glucose mobilization, especially for brain). The master rule: high cortisol shortly after waking, low cortisol in the hours before and early hours of sleep. Disrupted rhythm — not necessarily chronically elevated cortisol — drives burnout, poor sleep, brain fog, and immune issues.

Huberman maps four circadian cortisol phases (minimal secretion 4 h pre–2 h post lights-out; preliminary nocturnal rise hours 3–5 of sleep; main secretory phase hours 6–8 of sleep tied to REM; cortisol-awakening-response in the first 60–90 min after waking). Morning stack to raise cortisol: morning-sunlight-protocol (10+ min outdoor light, 10,000 lux if artificial), hydration, delay-caffeine-protocol (60–90 min post-wake), morning exercise, optional deliberate cold (not for everyone). Evening stack to lower cortisol: dim/amber lights, no screens, caffeine cutoff ~2 PM, physiological-sigh-stress, starchy carbs at last meal, avoid late intense training without recovery rituals.

Supplements (behavior first): ashwagandha 300–600 mg evening only (11–29% cortisol reduction); apigenin/magnesium threonate in huberman-sleep-stack for evening cortisol/GABA. Two early-phase-burnout vs late-phase-burnout patterns with distinct fixes. Chronic stress flattens the curve (hippocampal degeneration, cognition loss); sharp morning peak + steep afternoon decline predicts better health outcomes.
key_insights: Cortisol = energy deployer — releases liver/muscle glucose; crosses blood-brain barrier; fuels hippocampus and cognition; distinct from fast adrenaline.
Rhythm > absolute level — many problems are mistimed cortisol, not "too high" all day.
You wake because cortisol rises — CAR is the daily anchor; first hour is the only chance to amplify morning peak until next day.
Sleep length matters for phase 3 — 6 h sleep truncates the steep pre-wake cortisol rise; 8 h gets full REM-linked surge.
Evening spike poisons morning — stress/exercise/caffeine in phase 1 (4 h before–2 h after sleep) suppresses next-morning CAR via HPA negative feedback → sluggish mornings → more caffeine.
Stack protocols by time of day — morning tools raise; evening tools lower; apply at your main pain point first.
Low-carb transition — cortisol shifts up ~3 weeks on <30% carb diet, then normalizes; starchy evening carbs keep cortisol low via glucose feedback to hypothalamus.
Late workout recovery — post-gym: starchy carbs, long-exhale breathing, hot shower/sauna, dim lights — not cold blast or phone.
Burnout type 1 — morning anxiety/stress → afternoon crash → NSDR on waking, hydrate, bright light, delay caffeine.
Burnout type 2 — morning fog → evening wired/tired → focus on 6 h pre-sleep + 2 h post-sleep cortisol suppression stack.
Flattened curve = bad — aging, menopause, cancer survivorship literature links blunted morning peak + slow afternoon decline to worse outcomes; practices that restore peak/trough help.

videos.title: Controlling Your Dopamine for Motivation, Focus & Satisfaction | Huberman Lab Essentials
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman Huberman Lab Essentials recap (~33 min, 555K views) of controlling-dopamine-motivation-focus-satisfaction-huberman — the condensed, tool-forward cut of the 137-minute dopamine masterclass. Same core thesis: dopamine is a baseline + peak currency for motivation, craving, time perception, and movement — not a "pleasure hit." Your drive depends on current dopamine relative to recent history; after any peak, baseline drops below where it started (depleted vesicle pool).

Covers: neuromodulator vs neurotransmitter; substantia nigra → dorsal striatum (movement) vs mesocorticolimbic (reward/motivation); synaptic vs volumetric release; stimulus magnitudes (chocolate 1.5×, sex 2×, nicotine/cocaine 2.5×, amphetamine 10×, enjoyed exercise ~2×); evolutionary foraging frame; intermittent-dopamine-schedules and reward prediction error; caffeine as D2/D3 upregulation exception + yerba mate neuroprotection; amphetamine/cocaine plasticity damage (2003 study); cold-water-dopamine (2.5× sustained rise); dopamine-from-effort (Stanford gold-star study, growth mindset); taste-reset sugar studies; supplements (Wellbutrin, L-tyrosine, PEA + Alpha-GPC); social connection as dopamine pathway input.

Omitted vs full episode: dopamine-stacking, smartphone-at-gym rule, melatonin/10 PM–4 AM light warnings, Mucuna/huperzine A, 14-tool enumeration, and deeper Lembke pleasure-pain integration — see the full source.

Best use: quick review or first pass before the 137-min masterclass; pairs how-to-increase-motivation-drive-huberman-essentials for the complementary wanting-vs-liking / here-and-now-molecules angle.
key_insights: Motivation is relative — Baseline vs recent peaks dictates quality of life and pursuit drive; repeated indulgence raises enjoyment threshold.
Post-peak trough — After reward, dopamine drops *below* pre-seeking level; addiction = chasing relief from depletion, not pleasure.
Intermittent beats constant — Don't expect max dopamine every session; casino/social-media variable reinforcement preserves long-term motivation.
Caffeine exception — Upregulates D2/D3 receptors; yerba mate adds caffeine + antioxidants + GLP-1 + dopamine-neuron neuroprotection.
Cold water paradox — Unlike most peaks, cold immersion can raise baseline for hours (2.5×); novelty required — adaptation dulls effect.
Effort-as-reward — External rewards (gold stars, trophies) dissociate pleasure from activity; prefrontal reframing during friction builds reflexive drive.
Don't spike before or after effort — Learn dopamine release *from* effort itself; trophy-focus extends time-perception and drains in-activity pleasure.
Supplements are episodic — L-tyrosine (500–1000 mg, peak ~45 min, crash after); PEA 500 mg + Alpha-GPC 300 mg for short focus bouts; avoid regular use.

videos.title: Controlling Your Dopamine For Motivation, Focus & Satisfaction
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary: andrew-huberman "Dopamine Masterclass" (~137 min, 12.3M views). Thesis: dopamine is not a "hit" molecule — it is a baseline + peak currency for motivation, craving, satisfaction, and time perception. After any big peak, baseline drops (tonic vs phasic release; depleted vesicle pool). dopamine-stacking across unrelated activities (work hard / play hard) silently erodes drive. Fourteen tools to sustain motivation without addiction: intermittent-dopamine-schedules, avoid stimulants every session, dopamine-from-effort (reward friction not trophy), cold-water-dopamine (250% sustained rise), highly-palatable-food-reset (48 h), limit melatonin and 10 PM–4 AM light, cautious supplement use (Mucuna, L-tyrosine, PEA, huperzine A). Caffeine upregulates D2/D3 receptors — exception among pre-activity stimulants; yerba mate may protect dopamine neurons. Pleasure-pain balance per Anna Lembke's *Dopamine Nation*.
key_insights: No "dopamine hits" — Experience depends on current baseline vs recent peaks, not absolute release. Repeated indulgence raises your enjoyment threshold.
Peak → baseline drop — Post-marathon / postpartum / post-win crashes are dopamine baseline drops proportional to peak height. Addiction = progressive narrowing of what still releases dopamine.
pleasure-pain-balance — Pleasure is followed by sub-perceptible "pain" (craving) because the readily releasable vesicle pool is depleted; chasing the peak again lowers baseline further.
One currency — Chocolate + alcohol + intense exercise + social media + sex all draw from the same dopamine budget across the week.

intermittent-dopamine-schedules — Casino-style variable reinforcement preserves motivation; flip-a-coin whether to bring music/pre-workout/phone into gym. Don't spike before or after effort — spike from effort.
Smartphone layering — Phone during workouts/life layers dopamine sources and dulls the underlying activity (Huberman's personal rule: no phone in workouts this year).
Stimulant trap — Pre-workout drinks, Adderall/Ritalin/modafinil before every study/workout session eventually undermine motivation for that activity (caffeine excepted via receptor upregulation).

cold-water-dopamine — ~14°C water up to neck for up to an hour → 250% dopamine above baseline sustained ~3 hours (European Journal of Physiology); comparable peak to cocaine without crash; raises baseline long-term.

dopamine-from-effort — Stanford nursery-school study: external gold-star rewards reduced intrinsic drawing. Growth mindset = access dopamine during friction via prefrontal reframing ("this pain is the good part").
Belief validation releases dopamine — Hearing confirming information activates dopamine (Neuron 2021); knowledge of fasting benefits can amplify fasting adherence.

Supplements — Mucuna pruriens (L-DOPA) = intense + crash; L-tyrosine 500–1000 mg peaks ~45 min then drops; PEA + Alpha-GPC for short focus bouts; huperzine A via cholinergic-dopaminergic cross-talk. Avoid melatonin for sleep (lowers dopamine ~60 min); avoid bright light 10 PM–4 AM (multi-day dopamine suppression per Samer Hattar).

videos.title: Anti-Aging Expert: Creatine Is The Fat Loss Secret Doctors Don't Tell You - Dr. Darren Candow
videos.creator: darren-candow
videos.summary:
76-minute the-diary-of-a-ceo interview (~2.1M views, Jun 2025) with darren-candow — professor and Director of the Ageing Muscle and Bone Health Laboratory at the University of Regina; 175+ papers, 120+ on creatine alone; incoming VP of the International Society of Sports Nutrition. Thesis: creatine (discovered 1832) is the most researched supplement on earth — cheap, exceptionally safe, and far broader than gym bro muscle myths. It's one tool in a health toolbox where weight training is the hammer and creatine is the multi-purpose wrench.

Core reframes: debunk creatine-myths-debunked (kidney false positives from elevated creatinine, transient water retention from loading, not men-only, no hair-loss evidence, cramps reduced via super-hydration). creatine-dosing-by-benefit — ~5 g/day for muscle; 8–12 g for bone (with resistance training); brain healthy at ~10 g safety net but stressed brains (sleep deprivation, jet lag, exams) may need 20–30 g acutely because creatine struggles through the blood-brain barrier. Only creatine-monohydrate + third-party tested (CreaPure, NSF) — gummies OK if verified (James Smith found ~90% of shelf products had no creatine). Fat loss is indirect via lean mass; meta-analyses show reduced fat mass in females. Alzheimer's (20 g × 8 weeks → +11% brain creatine), depression adjunct (5 g + SSRI doubled remission in one trial), concussion prophylaxis emerging. Candow personally takes ~10 g/day baseline, 20–25 g after jet lag; timing irrelevant.
key_insights: ATP + Robin metaphor — Batman is ATP; creatine (Robin) replenishes energy currency during high-intensity work; body synthesizes 1–3 g/day in liver + brain only; 95% stored in muscle
Vegans respond best — no dietary creatine from animal flesh; supplementation fills the gap most dramatically
Loading optional — 4×5 g/day saturates fast but causes GI issues + transient water; 3–5 g/day for ~30 days reaches same muscle saturation without bloat
Microdosing tolerability — split doses (morning + workout bottle) avoids dizziness from methyl-group → adrenaline synthesis on empty stomach
Performance > hypertrophy — ~1.2 kg lean mass gain over 8 weeks; only ~half is skeletal muscle; main robust effect is training volume / recovery
Bone needs exercise + higher dose — 8–12 g with weight training slowed hip BMD loss in postmenopausal women (2-year trial); never shown without exercise
Brain stress dosing — healthy rested brain likely makes enough; sleep-deprived (21 hr) study used 30 g bolus; Stroop test 90 min + 20 g improved cognition; don't mega-dose daily long-term
Toolbox hierarchy — hammer = weight training; screwdriver = cardio/sleep; wrench = creatine; protein force-multiplier when combined
Sarcopenia — ~1% muscle/year + 1–3% strength/year after 40 for sedentary; resistance training plateaus decline; never too late to start (80–100 still benefit)
Menopause link — estrogen implicated in creatine synthesis enzymes; postmenopausal women strong responders for bone/muscle/brain
Kids/adolescents — reviews suggest safe at recommended doses; ≥1 g/day for bone + muscle development (consult doctor)
Safety at scale — 25,000+ case review: even >10 g/day for years safe; timing of day irrelevant (paper accepted "two days ago" per recording)
Fat loss title caveat — indirect via metabolic health + lean mass; not a fat burner like caffeine
Consistency beats dose perfection — place powder where coffee lives; effects subtle over weeks not hours

videos.title: A CS Professor on Why Slow Learning Wins in the AI Era | CU Boulder, Tom Yeh
videos.creator: tom-yeh
videos.summary:
13-minute interview with tom-yeh, CS professor at the University of Colorado Boulder and founder of ai-by-hand — a global initiative to demystify AI by writing out math by hand. Yeh missed deep learning as a student (too old for the wave), then had to relearn from scratch as a professor when everyone shifted to neural nets. His AI by Hand project documents that journey: drawing transformers token-by-token until the math clicks.

Core thesis: learning-by-hand-human-pace reconnects learners to human speed and ownership. When he taught intro C++ on a blackboard instead of live-coding, three things happened — he could only write at human speed, students could only follow at human speed, and copying notes by hand kept phones out of Instagram. "Having an answer doesn't mean you know it" — AI and purchased credentials are artifacts, not learning-ownership-not-answers.

Against the hype cycle: tools change every few years (DeepSeek → Google Cloud supercomputer) but evergreen-foundational-skills persist — matrix multiplication from Jurassic Park CGI through big data, ML, AI, and likely quantum computing; transformers will still matter when today's hot model is forgotten. The Gyeongbokgung palace metaphor: burned down in the 1500s except the rock foundation; rebuilt in the 1800s on the same base — foundation-over-trendy-tools.

Your piano or soccer practice is not wasted — learning-meta-skill-transfer means the *process* of acquiring hard skills becomes identity. Skip one AI tool, fine; skip your next piano lesson, not fine. Chegg died to ChatGPT but students still cheat — ai-cheating-incentive-misalignment treats symptoms. Hire for work ethic, problem-solving, and teamwork; those people adopt AI automatically. "AI cannot change people — only you can change AI."
key_insights: AI by Hand — write/draw every step of transformer math; makes the black box approachable; resonated because struggle is visible
Blackboard C++ semester — human writing speed caps lecture pace; note-copying removes keyboards from social feeds; focus improves
Answer ≠ knowledge — degrees, certificates, and AI outputs are proof artifacts; ownership requires time invested proportional to value
Evergreen vs trendy — matrix multiplication recurs across CGI, big data, ML, AI, quantum; DeepSeek hype fades, transformer foundations endure
Palace foundation metaphor — Gyeongbokgung rebuilt on 1500s rock base after fire; skills on solid foundations survive tool obsolescence
Meta-skill > current tool — piano/soccer patience transfers; Yeh caught up on deep learning from far behind using his breakdown-by-hand method
Skip the tool, not the practice — one AI product obsolete next year; abandoning disciplined skill practice erodes who you are
Willingness differentiates — not memorizing transformer equations forever, but proving you can take on hard learning challenges
Chegg → AI didn't fix cheating — symptom removal; root cause is incentive system that doesn't reward real learning investment
Hire character, tools follow — problem solvers learn AI on their own; team players use AI for collaboration; AI won't make a non-team-player collaborative

videos.title: Stanford Neuroscientist: Can't Remember Your Dreams? Your Brain May Be Warning You! - Dr David Eagleman
videos.creator: david-eagleman
videos.summary:
93-minute the-diary-of-a-ceo interview (~3.2M views) with david-eagleman — Stanford neuroscientist, Neosensory/BrainCheck cofounder, author of *Livewired*. Central thesis: you are not one rational self but a team-of-rivals-brain — competing neural networks whose "vote" changes by context. neuroplasticity-mechanisms never fully shuts off; the brain stops changing mainly because it thinks it already has the world modeled (fluid-vs-crystallized-intelligence). Growth requires attention-intense-challenges in the frustrating-but-achievable zone — drop sudoku once you're good; build cognitive-reserve-challenge against degeneration.

Dreams: Eagleman's lab theory — dream-visual-cortex-defense — REM blasts random activity into visual cortex every ~90 min to defend visual territory from takeover by hearing/touch during darkness (Harvard blindfold: takeover begins in ~60 min). Correlates across 25 primate species: more plastic brains → more dream sleep. Most dream content is noise; meaning is post-hoc like a random bookshelf sentence.

Habits & willpower: ulysses-contract-behavior — constrain future-you (clear alcohol, commit to 7 AM runs with Bob). anterior-mid-cingulate-cortex-willpower enlarges with history of hard unwanted work (not extending enjoyed tasks). Novice juggling = whole brain on fire; expert = less activity — brain's goal is efficiency.

AI: Cyber-optimist for kids — curiosity-driven Q&A sticks via plasticity cocktail vs "just in case" schooling. vicious-vs-virtuous-friction — outsource busywork (calculator era), never outsource thinking-through novel problems. Copy-paste AI answers = no learning + effort-phenomenon-ai red flags. Use AI as Aristotle-in-pocket for curious domains; ask "why am I wrong?" jagged-intelligence — AI inspired by brain but one-trial learning, emotion, and inner life differ. live-experience-renaissance — post-AI demand for in-person talks, live music, human hand-holding in care.

Perception & society: aphantasia-hyperphantasia-spectrum — population evenly spread; Pixar animators often aphantasic; accomplishes nothing predictive. novelty-familiarity-sweet-spot — hits need familiar anchors + novelty (radio repetition curve). Dialogue skills + complexifying out-groups to keep social circuitry alive; dementia prevention = stay challenged until death.
key_insights: Know thyselves — retrospective regret = different neural "party" was driving
Brain peaked at age 2 for synaptic count; pruning + crystallized intelligence follow
Challenge zone — frustrating but achievable; pandemic forced useful model updates
Religious Orders Study — nuns with Alzheimer's pathology but no symptoms → cognitive reserve from lifelong social/chore challenge
Retirement risk — shrink social circles + stop building pathways → cognitive decline
Exercise — rat data: wheel running increases neurogenesis trickle; sleep/diet matter
Social media unknowns — no valid control group; internet = bigger intellectual diet + curiosity plasticity
AI teaching pivot — critical thinking + creativity only durable curriculum
Creativity = remix — AI generates; humans select; humor punchlines still weak
One-trial learning — humans vs AI's millions of examples
2027 book — *The Ulysses Contract* on behavior change

videos.title: Fatty Liver Expert: The Toxic Ingredient Silently Filling Your Liver With Fat - Dr David Unwin
videos.creator: steven-bartlett
videos.summary:
steven-bartlett interviews david-unwin on *The Diary Of A CEO* (~2h11m, 3.6M views, May 2026). NHS GP (40+ years, north of Liverpool); NHS Innovator of the Year 2016; co-author of BMJ Open's most-read paper on low-carb T2D remission. 157 patients into drug-free type 2 diabetes remission via diet. Thesis: a pandemic of poor metabolic health — young people with T2D, normalized "dad bod," ~⅓ of global T2D undiagnosed; every year of poorly controlled T2D costs 100 days of life.

Mechanism chain: excess carbohydrate → insulin pushes glucose into cells → stored as belly fat + fatty-liver-long-silent-scream (~10 silent years, Roy Taylor) → insulin resistance → pancreas cranks more insulin → fat in pancreas → T2D. High glucose damages arterial glycocalyx within 6 hours. Eight cancers linked to diabetes; diet is #2 cause after smoking.

Clinical data (Unwin practice): prediabetes → 93% normal blood sugar on low carb; early T2D → 73%; after 5 years → 50%. Stitch in time.

Communication tools: teaspoons-of-sugar-equivalent — glycemic load recalculated as 4g teaspoon cubes (cornflakes 8, potato 9, banana 6, chocolate 7.5, 150g boiled rice 10); Public Health Collaboration infographics in 35 languages. starch-as-glucose-education — starch = glucose molecules holding hands; bread/rice/cereal are sugar. Only one sugar cube in entire 5L blood at normal levels — banana doubles Unwin's CGM reading.

Behavior change: wife Jen's grin-behavior-change-model (Goals, Resources, Increments, Notice) replaces doctor-as-leaflet; hope over moaning. food-addiction-abstinence-protocol — honesty → identify trigger foods → abstinence plan (moderation fails addicts); policing loved ones → deception. ultra-processed-food-addiction (~14% population; Jen Unwin's research; bread-from-bin-with-bleach case study). glp1-semaglutide-caution updated: Ozempic + CGM + low carb helped patient who couldn't moderate but could abstain.

Screening: waist-height-string-test — waist < half height (string test). healthspan-sick-years-gap — UK/US widening: ~23 sick years at end of life; £7,000/yr UK taxpayer cost of UPF consequences. Magnesium deficiency (soil depletion); citrate vs glycinate/threonate by bowel/sleep need.
key_insights: Health futures framing — everyone has multiple possible futures; lifestyle picks which; young people have longest runway but worst trends
Maturity-onset diabetes renamed — T2D in under-55s was unknown in 1986 Unwin practice; now patients under 25
Insulin as storage hormone — pushes glucose out of blood into cells; excess → fat (belly + liver); not just "middle-age spread"
Mrs. Jones epiphany (2012) — patient off metformin via low carb; "bread is sugar"; 40,000 online learners rubbished by professionals; Unwin ashamed
GP payment incentive — metformin compliance quotas part of pay; conflict with patient-led remission
2013 Monday-night cohort — 18 volunteers + Unwin + Jen + nurse Heather (unpaid); liver function improved 33–50% in weeks; weight, BP, HbA1c followed; hunger vanished
Eat less move more failure — Unwin blamed patients 25 years; All-Bran + skim milk advice; Belsen analogy shame; exercise undervalued until low carb
Nutrition literacy gap — successful adults ask if 12" pizza beats Nando's chicken; Premier League star thinks carbonara is health food from carb-loading era
Sugar all day — cereal + OJ + snacks + sandwich + cake + pizza = sugar on sugar; snacking epidemic; thin kids on snacks lack protein
Dried fruit trap — 60–70% sugar marketed as fruit; nova-food-classification halo
Orange juice / smoothies — fast sugar hit → insulin spike → crash → hunger; Unwin's biscuit panic-attack loop
White chocolate ~80% sugar — chocoholics addicted to sugar not cocoa; 90% dark ~2 tsp vs milk chocolate
Label reading — UK carbs exclude fiber (US includes); 4g carbs ≈ 1 tsp sugar; barbecue sauce ~30 cubes/bottle; real food > packets
Carb hunger paradox — more carbs → hungrier; fasting/keto → hunger vanishes; Christmas cake becomes "not food"
Keto as spectrum — tailor to goals (brain clarity, aesthetics, strength, healthspan); patients drift lower over time
Steven's GRIN demo — dad's stair-climbing limitation as health goal; consistency > six-pack deadline; WhatsApp fitness accountability league
Addiction deception — policing → hidden wrappers; Jen hid tray-bake evidence; gentle support beats judgment
Ozempic as partial answer — quiets cravings; not root cause; triple therapy (low carb + CGM + GLP-1) for severe cases
Carb creep consequences — remission patient returned with two amputated toes
Diet-cancer link — hyperinsulinemia inhibits apoptosis; fructose → tumor lipids; CRP inflammation; prevention underweighted vs treatment
Magnesium story — cow staggers from grass deficiency; patient seizures from deficiency + meds; serum Mg misleading
Screening ethics — actionable results only; scare without plan wastes NHS appointments
Real-world evidence — Unwin's NHS allocation (not cherry-picked wealthy patients); replicated in AU/NZ/NA

videos.title: How Different Diets Impact Your Health | Dr. Christopher Gardner
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
keywords: twin study vegan vs omnivore gardner
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman hosts christopher-gardner (~170 min, 265K views) for a wide-ranging nutrition debate that converges on food quality and patterns over diet tribalism. Thesis: humans are resilient — Tarahumara (corn/beans) and Inuit (whale/blubber) both thrived on indigenous diets; the standard American diet fails because of ultra-processed, convenient, hyper-palatable food. No one-size-fits-all diet, but shared basics: eliminate or drastically reduce processed food, prioritize fiber, consider low-sugar fermented foods, and fix the food supply (not just individual labels).

Diet diversity & genetics. Lactose persistence (northern European lactase) is the clearest diet-gene example. Gardner's raw-milk trial (n=16): 50% of self-reported lactose-intolerant subjects failed hydrogen breath test — symptoms real but mechanism may differ (e.g. SIBO). Raw milk did not cure intolerance vs conventional milk.

Processed food / NOVA. nova-food-classification cosmetic additives (150+ molecules) may add harm beyond macros, but isolating single dyes in human RCTs is nearly impossible (cardiometabolic outcomes move in weeks, cancer takes decades). Banning all additives would remove ~60% of grocery items without replacements — cruel for time-poor families. US vs Europe: same brands, different formulations (Nutella, Froot Loops dyes). Policy lever: industry reformulation, not consumer label literacy alone. Gardner has taken industry funding (avocado, soy, Beyond Meat) with equipoise designs; registers trials on clinicaltrials.gov.

DIETFITS & equipoise. diet-equipoise-studies — 600 people, 1 year, low-carb vs low-fat, both healthy (no added sugar/refined grain in either arm). No average weight-loss difference; massive within-group variance (–60 to +20 lb). Insulin-resistance and 3-SNP genotype did not predict who lost more. Follow-up keto vs Mediterranean: both lowered HbA1c; keto ↑ LDL, ↓ triglycerides; adherence collapsed on keto. Gardner's synthesis across studies: whole-food-plant-based-pattern (mostly plants; can include 10–30% animal).

Protein debate. Huberman (~1 g/lb lean mass) vs Gardner (RDA 0.8 g/kg = 2 SD above nitrogen-balance average; Americans already ~1.2 g/kg from food alone). Key reframes: protein-rda-vs-popular-targets — no protein storage depot (excess → deaminated → glucose); plants contain all 20 amino acids (complementarity myth); quality matters only at low total intake; no clinical protein deficiency in vegans except total calorie deficiency.

Twin study (Netflix). twin-study-vegan-vs-omnivore-gardner — 22 pairs, 8 weeks, fed 4 wk then cook-at-home. Vegans: ↓ LDL, ↓ fasting insulin, slight weight loss; exploratory: epigenetic clocks, telomeres, microbiome favored vegan. DEXA lean-mass loss featured in documentary was n=4 pairs, not in JAMA paper. Critique from Peter Attia on pattern vs single-variable science — Gardner: when testing food-pattern-vs-single-variable-nutrition, vegan vs omnivore *must* differ in fiber, B12, saturated fat, etc.

Fermented foods. fermented-food-inflammation-study — 6 servings/day low-sugar fermented food (yogurt, kefir, kombucha, kimchi, sauerkraut) for 10 weeks: ↑ microbiome diversity, ↓ 20/90 inflammatory markers. High-fiber arm: no avg diversity gain; fiber-microbiome-diversity-prerequisite — low baseline diversity → fiber can worsen inflammation (exploratory n=18).

Systems change. protein-flip-diet at CIA; Menus of Change (24 principles); Michelle Obama school food backlash → chefs in schools (Eat REAL, ~1M kids); mid-size diverse farms vs mega-monocrop; less meat, better meat (CAFO critique); taste-first institutional change (50%+ US meals eaten outside home).
key_insights: Resilience, not one best diet — indigenous extremes work; processed global diet does not.
Experience is data — respect gluten/dairy symptoms even when tests are ambiguous; celiac often undiagnosed.
NOVA is useful but blunt — turmeric/pectin can classify as ultra-processed; reformulation > blanket ban.
Equipoise beats headlines — kick-ass diet A vs crappy diet B explains nutrition "contradictions."
DIETFITS null average — genotype/insulin-resistance probes failed; healthy low-carb ≈ healthy low-fat for weight loss.
Plant-based ≠ Gardner's plant-based — his term = mostly plants + optional meat; recent usage = vegan (polarizing).
Protein craze overshoot — RDA already buffered; Americans exceed it; excess stored nowhere.
Plants aren't incomplete — all amino acids present; grains low lysine / beans low methionine at extreme restriction only.
Fermented foods > fiber alone (in this study) for inflammation — but fiber helps those with high baseline diversity.
Scale through chefs & schools — not Stanford-only elitism; CIA graduates nationwide in hospitals, hotels, districts.
Huberman converts — started daily low-sugar fermented foods after Sonnenberg study; endorses protein flip naming.

videos.title: Do THIS to Make $10,000 as a Student
videos.creator: mark-tilbury
videos.summary:
mark-tilbury (22 min, 888K views, Apr 2026) argues the fastest path to $10,000/month for students and beginners is becoming a digital architect — selling high-value digital services online — rather than following the traditional grades → university → $5,473/month job path (survey of 70,000 bachelor's graduates). Sponsored segments: Odoo (invoicing/CRM) and a free virtual wealth event.

The framework is five "maxxing" steps: talent-maxxing (double down on natural strengths, not school-taught weaknesses), service-maxxing (pick a service that makes/saves businesses money or time), skill-maxxing (learn and earn simultaneously via a five-step loop), position-maxxing (sell outcomes not tasks — same work, 10× pricing), and brand-maxxing (profile authority to break past the 10K plateau toward 20K–100K+).

Case study: Mark's son left school at 18 wanting to be a videographer but felt "not ready." Following the loop, he sold video editing to a local caravan park, delivered under pressure, iterated with AI, systemized with invoicing — now earns well over $10K/month.
key_insights: "Digital architect" beats freelancer, employee (Joey archetype), and generic side hustles for income ceiling
University isn't bad if money isn't the goal — but it won't get you to $10K/month freedom on its own
Worst advice: improve weaknesses; school system enforces this for years
Fastest online path: sell a digital service aligned to talent + golden rules
Don't overcomplicate the offer — billion-dollar dreams block first steps; $10K/month is the realistic target
Real world is the best teacher — no amount of prep beats one paying client
Reliability (on-time, clear communication) beats being the most talented
AI in the loop: remove repetitive bottlenecks after delivery experience, not before first sale
Cold outreach without profile authority = ignored DMs; profile + targeted messaging scales past 10K

videos.title: Doing This (Almost) GUARANTEES You Get Hired In A Job Interview!
videos.creator: vinh-giang
videos.summary:
Vinh Giang's 6-minute clip on job interview preparation — specifically replacing adjective-heavy self-descriptions with a prepared origin story when answering "tell us about yourself." Shortlisted candidates aren't lucky; they're prepared when opportunity arrives. Vinh sourced a top 10 list of common interview questions from recruiter friend Jared (Australia), then argues most people still wing answers they already know will be asked.

The core technique: craft a 2–3 minute origin story — often a childhood memory — that reveals who you are, builds rapport, and links explicitly to the role. Vinh demos improvising for "Head of Innovation at Apple": 13-year-old wants love → dad says "no money, no honey" → discovers eBay → resells MP3 players → lifelong early-adopter pattern → Vision Pro, AI music tools, iPhone launch lines → therefore perfect for innovation leadership. The demo includes conversational hooks (asking the interviewer questions, humor) so the room shifts from interrogation to dialogue.

Storytelling triggers dopamine, endorphins, and oxytocin; after ~3 minutes the interviewer treats you as a friend, not a faceless candidate.
key_insights: Preparation = luck — define luck as preparation meeting opportunity; shortlisted people prepared, they didn't get lucky.
Top 10 questions are predictable — yet most candidates don't prepare answers (see top-10-interview-questions).
"Tell us about yourself" is always first — winging it fails on the question everyone knows is coming.
Adjectives fail — "integrity, honesty, punctuality" and "my weakness is perfectionism" don't connect; stories do.
Origin story format — 2–3 minutes; childhood or formative memory; show character; bridge to why you're right for *this* job.
Link story to role — the eBay/early-adopter thread maps directly to "Head of Innovation" requirements.
Make it conversational — ask the interviewer questions mid-story; humor and rapport beat Q&A stiffness.
Neurochemistry shift — storytelling releases dopamine, endorphins, oxytocin; interviewers relax and engage as peers.
Differentiation — stories separate you from hundreds of applicants who only list traits.

videos.title: Build Muscle & Strength & Forge Your Life Path | Dorian Yates
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
keywords: forty five minute twice week training
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman full episode (~167 min, 1.0M views) with dorian-yates — six-time Mr. Olympia and pioneer of high-intensity, low-volume training (Arthur Jones → mike-mentzer → Yates "Blood and Guts"). For the non-competitive person: forty-five-minute-twice-week-training (8–10 exercises, whole body, twice weekly) + good diet can transform health; competitive bodybuilders need more exercise selection but same intensity principle.

Core training loop: stimulate-recover-adapt-training — overload to real muscular failure (warm-ups + 1–2 working sets; drop set optional), then recover before returning. pump-vs-overload-myth — transient pump ≠ growth; progressive overload drives adaptation. training-deload-six-two-cycle — hard 5–6 weeks, submaximal 2 weeks (or 1 week fully off). Beginners: learn mechanics 2+ weeks before failure; mind-muscle link overrides cheating when sets get hard (mind-muscle-intentionality). Cardio separate from weights: air-bike-twenty-second-sprints (3×20 s all-out + recovery ≈6 min total) matches ~45 min steady-state in studies. laboratory-vs-practical-training — muscle-protein-synthesis lab timelines (hit muscle every 72 h) failed in Yates/Huberman real-world trials vs once-per-week body-part frequency.

Life arc: Birmingham council estate → detention center → documented every workout 1983–1997 → British champion on 3×/week ~45 min while working construction. natural-before-anabolics — 180→210 lb in ~18 mo natural; gear only when entering IFBB; steroid-merry-go-round warning for casual users. athlete-identity-retirement-crisis — retired at 35; "who am I?" → purpose shift to coaching/inspiration. Aging: Pilates/yoga/functional work restored posture (+1" height via alignment); deliberately lost muscle mass 250→230 lb on TRT for blood pressure/health; upper/lower 1×/week maintenance now.

Mind-body: DMT + ~20 ayahuasca ceremonies (Costa Rica camps) → psychedelics-oneness-perspective; cannabis daily 30+ years — cannabis-endocannabinoid-individual-variation (Yates 1/10 negative-risk swab vs wife paranoia); contrasts Huberman on how-cannabis-impacts-health-matthew-hill (Taskin 25-yr lung study, Rick Simpson oil, Madrid THC/cancer lab video). Sunlight essential — dopamine/pigmentation/metabolism through skin (morning-sunlight-protocol cross-link). women-resistance-training-same-rules — same overload/recovery rules; "toned" = muscle + fat loss; competitive bikini athletes on gear.
key_insights: Minimum effective dose — 45 min × 2/week enough for average 40–60 yr old if intensity + diet are right; time excuse "not relevant."
More volume failed experiment — Adding 4th day / extra sets stalled progress 3–4 weeks; cut back → growth resumed (documented logs).
One set to failure era — ~1991–92 Mentzer advice added another growth level; hybrid between pure HIT and conventional BB.
Steroid recovery gap — Champions recover faster; natural trainees need less total stimulus and more rest between sessions.
Diabetes reversal case — Client: 3×/week 45 min + low-carb month → out of diabetic/pre-diabetic range, fatty liver enzymes normalized.
TRT at 45 — Huberman and Yates both ~125 mg/week; get as far naturally first.
Top-five gate — 1990 Night of Champions: top 5 or quit competing and steroids.
Flexibility over rigidity — Mentzer too extreme (train every 10–12 days, cigarettes); Yates kept training for love of movement post-career.
Anger as fuel — Father died 13; channeled hardship; thick skin from punk/Oi background but quiet demeanor.
Women & muscle — ~1%/yr sarcopenia after 40; won't "bulk by accident" without genetics + drugs.

videos.title: EASY 3-Step Exercise To INSTANTLY Improve Your Articulation!
videos.creator: vinh-giang
videos.summary:
Vinh Giang's 3-minute live coaching clip on crisp articulation — why mumbled speech usually means the mouth is not moving enough, and how to fix it with deliberate over-pronunciation plus full-sentence energy. Vinh credits childhood speech-pathology training for his own clarity; he contrasts Australian mumbling ("good day mate") with the need to over-articulate in the US (which briefly made him sound "a little bit British").

The exercise has three parts: (1) overdo mouth movements and hit every syllable in live speech; (2) daily 5-minute book reading with the same exaggerated articulation — ignore anyone who says you sound too formal; (3) energize the entire sentence at healthy volume, using a count-to-10 drill where each number carries equal energy before applying it to a full question. A student demo shows the before/after: low motor volume and flat delivery → crisp, non-nasal articulation after both drills.
key_insights: Mumbling = small mouth movements — unclear speech is usually a physical articulation problem, not just "thinking too fast."
Over-articulation works immediately — exaggerating pronunciation in the moment produces audibly crisp results; it may feel theatrical but that is the point.
5 minutes daily with a book — sustained practice normalizes large mouth movements; sounding "British" or "trying too hard" is acceptable during training.
Volume and energy are part of articulation — low motor volume undermines clarity even when syllables are correct.
Sentence-level energy — most speakers lose energy mid-sentence (crackly vocal fry); maintain the same vitality from first word to last.
Count-to-10 equal-energy drill — each number at identical volume/energy trains consistent vocal presence before full sentences.
Nasality vs crispness — nasal tone ("when I talk I sound like this") is distinct from poor articulation; the demo student had neither after the drill.

videos.title: How to Enhance Focus and Improve Productivity | Dr. Cal Newport
videos.creator: andrew-huberman
videos.summary:
andrew-huberman hosts cal-newport (~178 min, 1.7M views) — Georgetown computer-science professor and author of *Deep Work*, *Digital Minimalism*, and *Slow Productivity* — for a buffet of focus/productivity tools rather than hard-and-fast abstinence rules. Huberman stays on social media, email, and phone; Newport models extreme disconnection — both paths are valid if you protect cognitively expensive work.

Core thesis: knowledge workers inherit pseudo-productivity metrics (visible busyness, meetings, email responsiveness) from agriculture/industry, while real value comes from deep-work-protocols — sustained, distraction-free cognitive effort. Smartphones impose task-switching-cost-cognition (network-switching is slow, energy-intensive) and solitude-deprivation (no time free from other minds' stimuli). Growth practice is deliberate-practice-vs-flow — maximal discomfort, not flow's time-dissolving ease.

Newport's top three protocols: (1) pull-based-workflow — fix your concentration budget in advance; pull tasks from an active list (Trello) instead of push-based email/meeting bombardment; (2) multiscale-planning — seasonal/quarterly objectives → weekly plan against real calendar → daily time-blocking-productivity (assign work to actual free hours, not abstract to-do lists); (3) shutdown-ritual-productivity — end-of-day loop closure, tomorrow preview, and a demonstrative "work is over" signal (Matt Walker sleep-association parallel: don't think about work at the dinner table).

Newport estimates ~4–4.5 hours/day of peak cognitive output — aligned with Huberman's ~3–4 h deep-work ceiling.
